features.title: queue-telemetry-freshness
features.proposalEvidence: `metrics/queue-telemetry.jsonl` — the per-PR detail log behind the `queueEfficiency` sensor's `review_coverage`/`first_pass_success_rate`/etc. sub-metrics — has exactly **one commit in its entire git history**: `1985638` (2026-09-23, "chore(metrics): optimize-implement-queue 2026-09-23", #5698), which added all 447 rows at once as a `new file`, spanning historical data from 2026-07-05 through 2026-09-21. `git log --all -- metrics/queue-telemetry.jsonl` confirms this is the only commit ever. Two subsequent daily `optimize-implement-queue` runs landed since (`446666e` #5718 on 2026-09-24, and today's `0f9ae0e` #5743) — neither touched the file at all, despite 51+ commits merging to `main` in that window (verified: `git log --oneline --since="2026-09-21" | wc -l` → 51). `.claude/skills/implement-queue/SKILL.md` documents the live path (`appendTelemetryRow` from `scripts/collect-queue-telemetry.mjs`, called by `scripts/orchestrate.mjs` at worker-completion time) and `scripts/reconcile-queue-telemetry.mjs` is wired into `optimize-implement-queue`'s own skill — but whichever of these is supposed to keep the committed file current, it visibly isn't.

features.title: Postgres RLS venue backstop
features.proposalEvidence: `docs/plans/2026-01-31-hospitality-platform-roadmap.md` § Phase 5+ lists `[ ] Row-Level Security` as an unbuilt future item. Verified 2026-09-07 that it's still unbuilt: no `ROW LEVEL SECURITY`/RLS references anywhere in `services/reservations/prisma` or `services/users/prisma`, and multi-tenant isolation today is entirely application-level — 39 route files under `services/reservations/src/routes` individually filter by `venueId` in their Prisma queries. Every one of those 39 call sites is a place a future route (agent-authored or human) could omit the filter and leak another venue's reservations/guests/deposits with no second layer of defense.

features.title: Human-touch classifier heuristics
features.proposalEvidence: `.claude/acmm/state.json`'s behavioral gates show `L6 human-touch-ratio: 73.1% < 50%` **FAIL (level capped)** — the only failing gate in today's audit (`node plugins/acmm/scripts/audit.js`, 2026-08-17), and it is what's blocking the platform from reaching ACMM L6. The classifier built to explain *why* agent PRs need human touches (`scripts/classify-human-touch.mjs`, shipped via the already-closed #3805/#3847 proposal) is live and recording data in `metrics/queue-telemetry.jsonl` — but of the last 19 classified `human_touch_reason` entries, **17 (89%) are `"other"`**, with only 1 `scope-change` and 1 `review-fix`. The taxonomy exists but its heuristics (merge-conflict markers, CI-failure-at-commit-time, prior-review-comment-count, scope-change language) aren't specific enough to explain the actual majority cause — so the L6-blocking metric has no actionable breakdown to optimize against.

features.title: human-touch reason telemetry
features.proposalEvidence: Today's ACMM audit (`.claude/acmm/state.json`, `plugins/acmm/scripts/audit.js`) shows the L6 behavioral gate `human-touch-ratio` at **73.1%** (n=26 merged agent PRs, 30-day window) against a required <50% — the only failing gate, capping the repo at L5 despite `agent-pr-revert-rate` (0.0%), `auto-qa-tuning-history` (3), and `agent-pr-acceptance` (100%) all passing comfortably. The gate measures merged agent PRs that required a non-author (human) commit before merge, but nothing in the sensor loop records *why* — was it a review-comment fix, a CI failure the agent couldn't resolve, a scope disagreement, a merge-conflict resolution? Without that breakdown, closing the gate is guesswork.
